subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these specific upstream GitHub Action revisions on workflows that handle app private keys, registry credentials, releases, security uploads, and Codex-agent execution?
rationale: The branch is a legitimate dependency refresh, but accepting new third-party action commits on privileged automation paths is an explicit supply-chain and operational-trust decision rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Approve the rebased revisions
options.body: A workflow/security owner verifies the upstream commits and their behavior on privileged callers, then approves the exact rebased head.

options.title: Split high-trust updates
options.body: Keep low-privilege workflow updates together but move token, release, Docker login, and Codex action revisions into separately reviewed dependency PRs.

options.title: Pause the group update
options.body: Close or defer this batch if the repository does not currently want to expand the trusted action revisions together.

recommendation.title: Approve the rebased revisions
recommendation.body: A workflow/security owner verifies the upstream commits and their behavior on privileged callers, then approves the exact rebased head.

likelyOwner.reason: They own acceptance of external workflow code that runs with repository credentials and release permissions.
